args.message:
Fix round_money to use ROUND_HALF_EVEN per FIN-212

The nightly build failed because tests/test_money.py expects banker's
rounding, but round_money was quantizing with ROUND_HALF_UP. Switch the
rounding mode to ROUND_HALF_EVEN so half-cent amounts (e.g. 2.665)
round to the nearest even cent, as required by FIN-212.

args.head: fix/FIN-212-bankers-rounding
args.title: Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212
args.body:
## Summary
The nightly build failed because `tests/test_money.py` expects banker's rounding for `round_money`, but `src/money.py` imported and used `ROUND_HALF_UP`, causing half-cent amounts like `2.665` to round the wrong way.

## Changes
- `src/money.py`: switch `round_money` from `ROUND_HALF_UP` to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` when quantizing to cents, matching the documented FIN-212 behavior.

## Verification
- CI run `ci-0001` on this branch passed, including the `round_money` tests.

transcript.reasoning_content:
The bug: uses ROUND_HALF_UP instead of ROUND_HALF_EVEN. Note 2.675 with binary... no, Decimal is exact: 2.675 quantize to 0.01 with HALF_EVEN → 2.68 (since digit before is 7, odd, round up → 2.68). 2.665 → digit before is 6 even → stays 2.66. Wait 2.665 → 2.66 or 2.67? Half-even: 2.665 → last kept digit 6 (even) → round down → 2.66. Correct.

Create branch, fix, commit, CI, PR.
